title: Health checks: liveness and readiness split
description:
Split the single /health endpoint into separate liveness and readiness probes for Kubernetes and load balancer compatibility.

Why this issue exists:
The current /health endpoint returns {status:ok} but does not distinguish between 'the process is alive' (liveness) and 'ready to serve traffic' (readiness). Kubernetes, ECS, and ALB all need both. A restarting daemon that is alive but not yet connected to Kubo should fail readiness without failing liveness.

Scope:
- GET /healthz/live — returns 200 if the process is running. Never depends on external services. Used by Kubernetes liveness probe.
- GET /healthz/ready — returns 200 only when all dependencies are up: Kubo reachable, SQLite migrations complete, gossipsub swarm joined. Returns 503 with JSON body listing failing checks during startup or degraded state.
- Keep GET /health as a backwards-compatible alias for /healthz/ready
- Add a structured JSON body to /healthz/ready: {status, checks: [{name, ok, detail}]}
- Document probe configuration for Kubernetes and ECS in RUNBOOK.md

Acceptance criteria:
- /healthz/live returns 200 immediately after process start, before Kubo connects
- /healthz/ready returns 503 if Kubo is unreachable
- /healthz/ready returns 200 once all checks pass
- Existing /health endpoint continues to work
